newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Makin quits directorships through illness.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Makin quits directorships through illness.

text.p: Former Clear Communications chief executive Andrew Makin has resigned all his directorships after learning he has terminal cancer, the New Zealand Herald reported on Wednesday.
Makin, who retired from Clear early this month, had recently been appointed to the boards of Sovereign Assurance and Morgan & Banks.
"I've had to resign from the boards I've been appointed to without even attending a meeting," Makin told the Herald.
His former staff were among the first to be told about Makin's future at an in-house meeting on Tuesday.
On Monday, Makin learned that the back pain which had marred his final months at Clear was due to cancer, not sciatica as previously diagnosed.
